statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-114583: tarfile.tar_filter did not reject a hard or symbolic link member whose name refers to the extraction destination itself (for example an empty name or "."), so such a member could replace the destination directory with a link and redirect later members outside it. Upstream issue: https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/160097, advisory: https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/43JOWPRAV5DI3VZ4FUEUAZOHCATXXOCK/ and CVE record: https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-114583. The fix, commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/e7e0b3523ad6ba8472873dda594cf4021a16f8b5 on main, adds to _get_filtered_attrs in Lib/tarfile.py a check that raises OutsideDestinationError for a link member whose normalised name is the destination (os.path.normpath(name) == os.curdir). The 3.11 backport is commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/bc93f8ad4c4a0f92d184ec8fccc8ff8a651dcec2 on the 3.11 branch, first released in 3.11.18. There is no 3.10 release with the fix; DHI backports the same Lib/tarfile.py change onto 3.10.22. Checked usr/lib/python3.10/tarfile.py in the python-3.10 package. The python-3.10-pycache-pyc0, -pyc1 and -pyc2 packages of each build carry tarfile .pyc files compiled with checked source hashes, and in every build their hash matches that build's tarfile.py, so Python revalidates them against that source at import, in every build of the python-3.10 source published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, 3.10.19-r0 to 3.10.22-r8, x86_64 and aarch64, checksums verified against the repository index. The check is absent in every build before 3.10.22-r5 and present in 3.10.22-r5 and every later build, on both architectures. The range ends at 3.10.22-r5, the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-114583 (PSF-2026-45): tarfile's "tar" extraction filter could be bypassed with crafted link members, including symlinks with empty or directory-like names, that replace the destination directory and redirect later members outside it, so tarfile.extractall(filter="tar") could write files outside the destination. It is the tar_filter counterpart of CVE-2026-7774. The fix adds a check to _get_filtered_attrs in Lib/tarfile.py that rejects a link member whose name normalizes to the destination directory under both the "data" and "tar" filters. On the 3.11 branch it is commit bc93f8ad4c4a0f92d184ec8fccc8ff8a651dcec2, first released in CPython 3.11.18; the CVE record lists every CPython release before 3.11.18 as affected. Sources: https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/bc93f8ad4c4a0f92d184ec8fccc8ff8a651dcec2, https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/160097, https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/43JOWPRAV5DI3VZ4FUEUAZOHCATXXOCK/, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-114583. We checked every published python-3.11 build for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository, 3.11.14-r0 to 3.11.18-r4 (24 builds), on x86_64 and aarch64, each against its index checksum: Lib/tarfile.py in the python-3.11 package and the compiled tarfile .pyc files in python-3.11-pycache-pyc0, python-3.11-pycache-pyc1 and python-3.11-pycache-pyc2. Both architectures agree in every build. Every build from 3.11.18-r0 ships the upstream 3.11.18 tarfile.py, which has the check; every earlier build lacks it. Some earlier builds ship a tarfile.py that differs from its upstream release; we compared each of those files with the upstream releases, and none of them adds this check. The .pyc files are hash-checked, and in every build each one carries the source hash of that build's own tarfile.py, so the compiled copies match the source checked. The range ends at 3.11.18-r0, the first build of CPython 3.11.18.

CVE-2026-114583: tarfile.tar_filter did not reject a hard or symbolic link member whose name refers to the extraction destination itself (for example an empty name or "."), so such a member could replace the destination directory with a link and redirect later members outside it. Upstream issue: https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/160097, advisory: https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/43JOWPRAV5DI3VZ4FUEUAZOHCATXXOCK/ and CVE record: https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-114583. The fix, commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/e7e0b3523ad6ba8472873dda594cf4021a16f8b5 on main, adds to _get_filtered_attrs in Lib/tarfile.py a check that raises OutsideDestinationError for a link member whose normalised name is the destination (os.path.normpath(name) == os.curdir). The 3.11 backport is commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/bc93f8ad4c4a0f92d184ec8fccc8ff8a651dcec2 on the 3.11 branch, first released in 3.11.18. There is no 3.10 release with the fix; DHI backports the same Lib/tarfile.py change onto 3.10.22. Checked usr/lib/python3.10/tarfile.py, which ships in libpython-3.10-stdlib up to 3.10.20-9 and in libpython-3.10-minimal from 3.10.20-10; no package of these builds carries a tarfile .pyc, in every build of the python-3.10 source published in the DHI Debian 13 repository, 3.10.20-0 to 3.10.22-8, amd64 and arm64 (3.10.20-0 to 3.10.20-2 were published as architecture-independent packages), checksums verified against the repository index. The check is absent in every build before 3.10.22-5 and present in 3.10.22-5 and every later build, on both architectures. The range ends at 3.10.22-5, the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-114583 (PSF-2026-45): tarfile's "tar" extraction filter could be bypassed with crafted link members, including symlinks with empty or directory-like names, that replace the destination directory and redirect later members outside it, so tarfile.extractall(filter="tar") could write files outside the destination. None of the scanned packages (libpython-3.15-minimal, libpython-3.15-stdlib, python-3.15 and python-3.15-minimal) ships a compiled tarfile .pyc. The range ends at 3.15.2-0, the first build of CPython 3.15.2.
